intro: Every command the toolkit carries, with the same action in each language. Python and Node.js bind to the same core and are not released yet, so their examples show the shape they will have.

entries.title: scan
entries.summary: Look for devices and report what answers.
entries.detail: The scan runs in every enabled mode. `scan_on` restricts it to the modes you name, and enables none that the configuration leaves out.

examples.rust:
let devices = govee.scan().await?;
let lan_only = govee.scan_on(&[Mode::Lan]).await?;
examples.python:
devices = await govee.scan()
lan_only = await govee.scan_on([Mode.LAN])
examples.node:
const devices = await govee.scan()
const lanOnly = await govee.scanOn(['lan'])

entries.title: devices
entries.summary: List the devices already known. It touches no network.
entries.detail: The `lan` cache answers from disk, so a device found once costs no scan on the next run.

entries.title: describe
entries.summary: Report what the device file declares for a model.
entries.detail: It reads no hardware. Use it to see the range of every argument before you send a value.

entries.title: status
entries.summary: Ask the device for its current state.
entries.detail: `last_status` returns the state already known and sends nothing.

examples.rust:
let state = device.status().await?;
let cached = device.last_status();
examples.node:
const state = await device.status()
const cached = device.lastStatus()

entries.title: watch
entries.summary: Follow events: a device appears, a mode changes health.

examples.python:
async for event in govee.events():
    print(event)

entries.title: doctor
entries.summary: Report everything wrong with the configuration.
entries.detail: Run it first when a device does not answer.

entries.title: power
entries.summary: Turn the device on or off.

examples.cli:
govee on living-room
govee off living-room

entries.title: brightness
entries.summary: Set the brightness of the whole device.
entries.detail: The device file carries the range. A value outside it is an error, never a clamp. On a verified model `0` is clamped by the firmware to `1` and does not turn the device off.

entries.title: color
entries.summary: Set one color for the whole device.

entries.title: color_temp
entries.summary: Set the white temperature, in kelvin.
entries.detail: It ends the color the device showed: white and color are two states that exclude each other. Where the mode carries the RGB rendering in the same frame, the core computes it and sends both.

entries.title: segment
entries.detail: One color fills every zone. A list of colors states one zone each, which is how a mode that addresses every LED is painted pixel by pixel: ask for the native resolution and pass that many colors. With a list of zones, the zones you name take the one color and the rest stay as they are; that needs a mode that paints by mask. A count the unit renders as a smaller one is refused, and the message names the counts it refines at.

examples.cli:
govee segment living-room "#ff3d00"
govee segment living-room --zones 1,2,3 "#ff3d00"
# One color per LED: 42 of them on this unit, in zone order.
govee segment living-room --resolution native "#ff3d00,#00a3ff,#000000,..."
# The same list, from a pipe or a file.
echo "#ff3d00,#00a3ff,#000000,..." | govee segment living-room --resolution native -

entries.title: music
entries.summary: Play an effect the device renders from its own microphone.
entries.detail: The device listens and nothing streams from your host. The effect identifiers belong to the mode: the same number names another effect over another mode, and `lan` carries no music command at all. Nothing stops the effect — set a color, a temperature or the power to end it.

examples.rust: device.music(&Music { effect: 3, sensitivity: 60, soft: false, color: None }).await?;

entries.title: open_stream
entries.summary: Open the segment channel and keep it armed.
entries.detail: The stream reports the zone count and the frame rate measured on the unit. It stays armed until you close it, and the colors end with it.

examples.cli:
# frames.txt: one frame per line, one color per zone.
govee stream living-room --resolution native < frames.txt
examples.rust:
let stream = device.open_stream(StreamOptions::default()).await?;
println!("{} zones at {} Hz", stream.zones(), stream.rate_hz());
examples.node:
const stream = await device.openStream()
console.log(stream.zones, stream.rateHz)

entries.title: set_zone
entries.summary: Set one zone of the stream.

examples.cli:
# One frame per line, one color per zone.
echo "000000,ff3d00,000000" | govee stream living-room --resolution 3

entries.title: set_all, fill and clear
entries.detail: `set_all` takes one color per zone. `fill` gives every zone the same color. `clear` sets them to black.

entries.title: close
entries.detail: A frame that a newer one replaces before it goes out is counted in `frames_superseded`. Nothing else disarms the channel.

examples.cli: # The stream ends when standard input ends.

entries.title: send
entries.summary: Send one entry of the device file, by name.
entries.detail: It works for a model this build has never heard of. The entry declares the type of every argument, and the range stays the core's to check. `read` is the same for an entry that returns an answer.

examples.node:
await device.send('brightness', { level: 40 })
const reply = await device.read('status', {})

entries.title: provision_wifi
entries.summary: Put a new device on a Wi-Fi network, over Bluetooth.
entries.detail: This is how a device out of the box becomes reachable over `lan`. The password travels in plaintext with no key exchange: anything in Bluetooth range while it runs can read it.

entries.title: Choose a mode
entries.summary: Restrict a command to one mode.
entries.detail: It never enables a mode the configuration leaves out, and it never falls back. A device that no enabled mode reaches is an error.

examples.rust:
let mode = device.serving_mode()?;
let health = device.health(Mode::Lan);
examples.node:
const mode = device.servingMode()
const health = device.health('lan')
